SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. 5422 (C)
S.1, Special Branch Exhibits 39
REPORT
Date August 12, 1939.
Subject Central European Jews - Articles in "China Weekly Review".
Made by D.S. Pitts. Forwarded by C. Crawford. S.I.

Mr. STANTON, American Executive Consul, has been interviewed in connection with the correspondence appearing in the enclosed communication from Mr. Paul KOMOR and his help solicited in an effort to curb any possible attempt by the "China Weekly Review" to hinder the relief work of the Emigrant Committees that might result from the publication of articles relating to the Refugee problem.

After the salient points of Mr. KOMOR's letter had been placed in Mr. STANTON's hands and the situation, as it affects the Police, explained to him, this gentleman communicated with Mr. J.B. POWELL, editor and publisher of the "China Weekly Review". Mr. POWELL stated that the articles for publications were not of a political nature and were of a character that could only be construed as being sympathetic towards the plight in which refugees are finding themselves, and as such, would, it was hoped, merit sympathetic understanding and treatment of the Refugee question by both the authorities and readers.

Mr. STANTON instructed Mr. POWELL to refrain from publishing any item that might cause unpleasantness to the Relief Committees, to which Mr. POWELL agreed.

D. S.
D.C. (Special Branch)

报告
日期：1939年8月12日。
主题：中欧犹太人——《密勒氏评论报》上的文章。
制作人：D.S. Pitts。转呈人：C. Crawford，特别课督察长（S.I.）。

已就附函中 Paul KOMOR 先生来信所涉及的通信事宜，约谈了美国执行领事 STANTON 先生，并请求其协助，以遏制《密勒氏评论报》可能因刊登有关难民问题的文章而阻碍移民委员会救济工作的任何企图。

在向 STANTON 先生出示 KOMOR 先生信函的要点，并向其解释涉及警方的情况后，这位绅士与《密勒氏评论报》的编辑兼出版人 J.B. POWELL 先生取得了联系。POWELL 先生表示，拟发表的文章并非政治性质，其性质只能被解读为对难民所处困境表示同情，因此希望当局和读者能对难民问题给予同情的理解与对待。

STANTON 先生指示 POWELL 先生避免刊登任何可能给救济委员会带来不快的内容，POWELL 先生对此表示同意。

D. S.
副督察长（特别课）

（左侧批注）：

S.M.P.
Shanghai

Dear Sirs:-

I beg to enclose copy of a letter addressed to
the Emigrants' Committee and the contents of which speaks
for itself.

Considering that there is sufficient inflamable
material in the world to-day and that we do not lack such
in Shanghai either and that the handling of the Emigrant
situation is difficult enough without superfluous
"New-stories" making things even more difficult, I hope
that you will be so good as to do what you can in the
sense of my letter to my Committee.

I am, Dear Sir,

Yours faithfully,

"I.C" RELIEF FUND
〔签名〕
Hon. Secretary & Treasurer

August 7th, 1939

Ellis Hayim, Esquire
E. Kann, Esquire
S. Kolen, Esquire
Shanghai

Gentlemen:-

Consul v. Randow has just 'phoned to me drawing
attention to the announcement appearing in the "China Weekly
Review" to the effect that a series of six articles which will
appear, beginning with the next number dealing with the Emigrant
question.

These articles will be supposed to show, why and
wherefore Emigrants came to Shanghai and it is to be supposed,
that they will not lack that journalistic sensationalism, which
seems to be an attribute to modern news-writing.

It is also stated in the announcement that the work
of the various Committees will be described, and it is therefore
to be assumed, that the writer of the series, a gentleman by
the name of Julius R u d o l p h (not registered with us) has
obtained or will attempt to obtain information from you or members
and organs of the Committee.

For reasons which I have frequently explained and
which have always been appreciated by the Committee, any
sensational propaganda work in connection with the Emigrants
question is to be tabooed as unnecessary and of no constructive
use. These questions, which are mainly political, are sufficiently
thrashed out in the world-press and need no further spreading
through any medium which could in any way be brought into
connection with our work which is absolutely only constructively
charitable and non-political.

Inasmuch as the German Consulate-General has given us
every possible support in very difficult circumstances, I would
very deeply regret if the "China Weekly Review" brought any
articles which would not be in keeping with the lines we have
ourselves laid down in connection with Propaganda, if any, for
the Emigrants.

I would therefore urge you to kindly look into this
matter without delay and to prevent, if possible the appearance
of any "new-stories" which might, in their effect, cause more
harm than any good at all.

Your early reply to this will be very much appreciated
Yours sincerely,
pages.zh:
1939年8月7日

Ellis Hayim 先生
E. Kann 先生
S. Kolen 先生
上海

诸位先生：

v. Randow 领事刚才致电给我，提请注意《密勒氏评论报》上刊登的一则公告，该公告称将连载六篇关于移民问题的文章，从下一期开始刊登。

据称，这些文章旨在揭示移民来到上海的原因和背景，并且可以预料，它们不会缺乏那种似乎是现代新闻写作特征的耸人听闻的手法。

公告中还称将描述各委员会的工作，因此可以推断，该系列文章的作者，一位名为 Julius R u d o l p h 的绅士（未在我处注册），已经或试图从你们或委员会成员及机构那里获取信息。

出于我经常解释且一直得到委员会认可的原因，任何与移民问题有关的耸人听闻的宣传作品都应被视为不必要且无建设性用途而予以禁止。这些问题主要具有政治性质，在世界报刊上已得到充分讨论，无需通过任何可能与我们的工作产生关联的媒介进一步传播，因为我们的工作绝对仅具有建设性的慈善性质，且非政治性。

鉴于德国总领事馆在非常困难的情况下给予了我们一切可能的支持，如果《密勒氏评论报》刊登的任何文章不符合我们就移民宣传（如果有的话）所制定的方针，我将深感遗憾。

因此，我恳请诸位立即调查此事，并尽可能防止出现任何弊大于利的“新闻故事”。

如蒙早日回复，不胜感激。

此致，

敬礼，

报告
日期 ____ 1939年10月3日。

主题 ____ “德籍犹太人中活跃的共产主义分子”——见于1939年9月30日《大陆新报》的报道。
制作人 ____ D.S. Pitts ____ 转呈人 ____ C. Gaspar [此处为手写签名]

附件报道的内容，说得委婉些，也是极度夸张的，因为在杨树浦地区向犹太难民分发共产主义宣传品的情况尚未发现任何实例。

众所周知的事实是，某些移民对难民援助委员会主要委员 Kurt MARX 博士等人给予他们的待遇表示了不满，同时各收容所和营地的管理人员也未能免受入住者的批评。

然而，将这类争吵 construed 为共产主义活动是大错特错的。虽然难民中可能存在一定数量的激进分子，但可以肯定的是，他们尚未通过散布任何形式的宣传品来显露其存在。

（左侧手写批注：C. 10月4日。）

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处处长办公室 * 1939年10月4日 *）

September 30, 1939.

TAIKIKU SHIMPO

COMMUNIST ELEMENTS ACTIVE AMONG GERMAN JEWS
IN YANGTSZEPOO DISTRICT

The number of German refugees
in Shanghai is reported to be now over 10,000. Several
thousand are residing in the Hongkew and Yangtszepoo
districts in the Japanese sector. A number of the
German Jews are communists and are reported to be actively
engaged in the dissemination of communist propaganda in
the Yangtszepoo District.

The Japanese authorities are
paying close attention to their movements.

1939年9月30日。

《大陆新报》

杨树浦地区德籍犹太人中
活跃的共产主义分子

据报道，目前在上海的德国难民人数已超过10,000人。数千人居住在日占区的虹口和杨树浦地区。部分德籍犹太人是共产主义者，据报道他们在杨树浦地区积极从事共产主义宣传品的散布工作。

日本当局正密切关注他们的动向。

Headquarters have approved of R. Weissenberg being
classified as a Police Watchman. He will be in uniform (Not
Armed) under the number 201 and employed at the Embankment
Building.

Supervision Fees are being paid by Mr. Henry H.
Cohen, 133 Yuen Ming Yuen Rd.

Although this man is employed in an Office in
Embankment Building, will you as a special case, have the
Officers on Day Patrol visit the Office and sign his Conference
Book in the forenoon and afternoon.

D. C. Polk

Shanghai, May 30th, 1939.

Our No.39/3973.

Henry H.Cohen Esq.,
133 Yuen Ming Yuen Road
Shanghai

Dear Mr. Cohen,

It gives me much pleasure in acknowledging
with thanks receipt of your kind letter concerning Mr. Robert
Weissenberg. I am more than grateful for your kind
suggestion and advice given on behalf of Mr. Robert Weissenberg.
I do realize the difficulties he or anybody else in his place
is facing in keeping out the crowd and allowing people admittance
to the various departments according to their respective needs.

Since you were good enough to offer us your
kind services for contacting the department concerned I would be
very thankful, if you would kindly take the necessary steps.
As to the expenses in connection I have gladly noted your kindness
and consideration.

With kindest regards and renewed thanks for
your sympathetic and active interest, I am

Very sincerely yours

Committee for the Assistance
of European Jewish Refugees in Shanghai
Disbursement and Housing
Committee.
Dr. Kurt Marx
Secretary.

亲爱的 Cohen 先生：

我很高兴收到您关于 Robert Weissenberg 先生的来信，并表示感谢。我非常感激您代表 Robert Weissenberg 先生提出的善意建议和指导。我确实理解他或处于他位置的任何人在阻挡人群并根据各自需求允许人们进入各个部门时所面临的困难。

既然您好心提出为我们联系相关部门，如果您能采取必要措施，我将不胜感激。关于相关费用，我已愉快地注意到您的好意和体谅。

致以最亲切的问候，并再次感谢您富有同情心和积极的关注，我是

您真诚的，

上海欧洲犹太难民援助委员会
支出与住房
委员会。
Dr. Kurt Marx
秘书。
